title: How to Find Custom Packaging Manufacturers for D2C Brands
description: Learn how to find, compare and evaluate custom packaging manufacturers in India. Discover what to check before placing your next packaging order.
heading: How to Find Custom Packaging Manufacturers for Your D2C Brand
body:
Finding the right packaging manufacturer is an important decision for any direct-to-consumer (D2C) brand. Your packaging affects product protection, shipping costs, customer experience and profit margins.

However, finding a suitable supplier can be surprisingly difficult. You may need to contact multiple factories, explain your requirements repeatedly, compare quotations with different specifications and request samples before placing an order.

Whether you need corrugated shipping boxes, premium mailer boxes, flexible pouches or printed sachets, a structured sourcing process can help you find the right manufacturing partner.

Here is how to approach packaging procurement for your D2C brand.

## 1. Identify the Right Packaging Format

Before contacting manufacturers, identify the type of packaging your product requires.

Different products have different protection, storage, shipping and presentation requirements.

| Packaging type | Common applications | What to consider |
|---|---|---|
| Corrugated boxes | Shipping, subscription boxes and bulk orders | Box dimensions, board strength and printing |
| Mailer boxes | Beauty, apparel, accessories and premium D2C products | Structure, opening experience and branding |
| Flexible pouches | Snacks, dry fruits, coffee and personal care | Material structure, barrier requirements and pouch format |
| Sachets and stick packs | Single-use products, samples and powders | Fill weight, sealing, material and pack dimensions |
| Bottles and containers | Cosmetics, beverages and personal care | Material, capacity, closure and compatibility |
| Labels | Bottles, jars, boxes and pouches | Adhesive, finish, printing and application surface |

The best format depends on your product, distribution method, required shelf life and budget.

If you are unsure which packaging format to choose, discuss your product and intended use with potential suppliers before finalising the design.

## 2. Find Manufacturers That Serve Growing Brands

Not every packaging manufacturer is suitable for every order.

Some factories specialise in large-volume industrial orders, while others may accommodate smaller batches and customisation requirements.

When evaluating suppliers, ask about:

- Minimum order quantity (MOQ).
- Experience producing your specific packaging format.
- Custom printing and finishing capabilities.
- Available materials and specifications.
- Sampling and prototype options.
- Production lead times.
- Delivery coverage and freight charges.
- Quality-control processes.

For an early-stage D2C brand, a supplier that accepts your required quantity and can maintain consistent quality may be more valuable than a larger factory offering a lower price only at very high volumes.

**Tip:** Confirm whether the quoted MOQ applies to each design, size, colour variation or combined order. These conditions can materially affect your actual procurement cost.

## 3. Compare Quotations on an Apples-to-Apples Basis

One of the most common packaging procurement mistakes is comparing prices without checking whether the underlying specifications are identical.

For example, two quotations for a corrugated box may differ in board construction, dimensions, printing coverage or finishing.

Likewise, flexible pouch quotations may differ in material structure, thickness, barrier properties, zipper specifications and printing method.

Before comparing suppliers, standardise the following information:

- Packaging type and dimensions.
- Material or board specifications.
- Printing requirements.
- Quantity per order.
- Additional features and finishes.
- Delivery location.
- Applicable taxes, freight and tooling charges.

Request a written quotation that clearly identifies what is included and what costs extra.

A lower unit price is not necessarily the lowest total cost if it comes with expensive freight, additional setup charges or higher minimum quantities.

## 4. Understand the Total Cost of Packaging

Packaging costs extend beyond the manufacturer's quoted unit price.

Depending on the packaging format and order, your total cost may include:

**Total procurement cost = packaging units + printing or setup charges + tooling or plates + freight + applicable taxes + other agreed charges.**

Some charges may be one-time costs, while others recur with every order.

For example, printing plates or custom dies may require an initial investment. Ask whether these charges apply to repeat orders and whether the manufacturer retains the tooling for future production.

For shipping boxes, also consider how the packaging affects volumetric shipping charges and product protection.

For flexible pouches, evaluate the material and barrier requirements alongside the unit price, especially when the packaging must protect products from moisture, oxygen or light.

## 5. Request Samples Before Committing to Bulk Production

A quotation confirms the proposed price and specifications, but it does not establish the final quality of the product.

Whenever practical, evaluate a sample before approving a large production run.

Check:

- Dimensions and fit.
- Material quality and consistency.
- Print accuracy and colour reproduction.
- Sealing and closure performance.
- Structural strength.
- Compatibility with your filling, packing and shipping processes.

For corrugated boxes, test the packaging with the actual product and intended shipping conditions.

For flexible pouches, confirm the seal integrity and suitability of the material for the product. Food-contact and other regulated applications may require additional documentation and testing.

Agree on the approved specifications and sample before authorising production.

## 6. Prepare a Complete Packaging Requirement

Manufacturers can usually assess your requirement more efficiently when you provide the essential details upfront.

For a corrugated box, include:

- Box style.
- Length, width and height.
- Quantity.
- Board specification, if known.
- Printing requirements.
- Delivery city.

For a flexible pouch, include:

- Pouch format.
- Dimensions and capacity, if known.
- Product to be packed.
- Material or barrier requirements, if known.
- Printing and closure requirements.
- Quantity and delivery city.

You do not need to know every technical specification before contacting a supplier. Clearly identify what you know and ask the manufacturer to recommend suitable options for the remaining details.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### How do I find a packaging manufacturer in India?

Start by identifying the packaging format, quantity, specifications and delivery location. Shortlist manufacturers with relevant production capabilities, compare quotations on identical specifications and evaluate samples before committing to bulk production.

### What is the minimum order quantity for custom packaging?

There is no universal MOQ. It depends on the packaging format, material, printing method, manufacturing setup and supplier. Ask each manufacturer for its minimum quantity for your exact design and specifications.

### Can startups order custom packaging?

Yes, some manufacturers work with startups and smaller D2C brands. Availability depends on the packaging type, production setup and order quantity. Confirm the MOQ and any setup charges before proceeding.

### How many manufacturers should I compare?

There is no fixed number, but comparing two or three detailed quotations can provide a useful starting point when the suppliers offer equivalent specifications. For specialised packaging, you may need a wider shortlist.

### What should I send a manufacturer to get an accurate quotation?

Share the packaging type, dimensions, quantity, material or board specifications if known, printing requirements and delivery location. Include a reference image or design file if available.

### Should I choose the cheapest packaging manufacturer?

Not automatically. Compare the complete landed cost, sample quality, production reliability, relevant capabilities and delivery commitments. The right supplier should meet your specifications at an acceptable total cost.

title: Custom Corrugated Box Prices: A Guide for D2C Brands
description: Understand what affects custom corrugated box prices, including board construction, dimensions, printing, order quantity and shipping.
heading: Custom Corrugated Box Pricing: What Should Your D2C Brand Expect to Pay?
body:
Corrugated boxes are widely used by D2C brands for shipping products, fulfilling ecommerce orders and protecting goods during transportation.

But how much should a custom corrugated box cost?

There is no single price that applies to every box. The cost depends on its dimensions, board construction, paper specifications, printing, order quantity, manufacturing process and delivery location.

Understanding these variables helps you compare manufacturers, prepare an accurate packaging budget and avoid paying for specifications your product does not require.

## 1. What Determines the Price of a Corrugated Box?

### Box dimensions

Larger boxes generally require more material, increasing their cost.

When requesting quotations, specify the required length, width and height. Also confirm whether the manufacturer expects internal or external dimensions.

If your product fits comfortably into a smaller box without compromising protection, reducing unnecessary packaging volume may lower both material and shipping costs.

### Board construction: 3-ply, 5-ply and 7-ply

Corrugated board consists of flat liner sheets and fluted paper layers.

Common constructions include:

| Construction | General characteristics | Potential applications |
|---|---|---|
| 3-ply | One fluted layer between two liners | Many lightweight products and general shipping applications |
| 5-ply | Two fluted layers with three liner sheets | Applications requiring greater cushioning or stacking performance |
| 7-ply | Three fluted layers with four liner sheets | Selected heavy-duty or demanding packaging applications |

These descriptions are general guidelines, not guarantees of box strength.

Actual performance also depends on paper grades, grammage, flute profiles, dimensions, manufacturing quality, moisture exposure and how the box is packed and handled.

Ask the manufacturer to recommend a suitable board specification for your product weight, stacking conditions and shipping environment.

### Paper quality and material consumption

Two boxes with the same external dimensions and ply count can have different prices.

Differences in liner paper, fluting paper, grammage and other material specifications can affect cost and performance.

Request the proposed board specification in writing so that you can compare quotations meaningfully.

### Printing and branding

Plain corrugated boxes are generally simpler to manufacture than boxes requiring more elaborate branding.

Depending on the design and production method, printing costs can be affected by:

- Number of printed sides.
- Number of colours.
- Ink coverage.
- Print method.
- Artwork complexity.
- Setup requirements.

If your packaging design allows it, ask manufacturers to quote both a simple branded version and a more elaborate version. This can help you evaluate the trade-off between presentation and cost.

### Box style and die-cutting

A regular slotted carton and a custom die-cut mailer box involve different manufacturing processes.

A regular slotted carton is a common shipping-box design with flaps that meet when closed.

A die-cut mailer box may offer a more tailored shape, integrated closing features or a more premium opening experience. However, custom cutting tools and more complex production can affect the initial cost.

Ask whether tooling charges are one-time costs and how they are treated on repeat orders.

### Order quantity

Manufacturers may offer different unit prices at different order volumes because setup costs and production efficiency vary.

However, the exact price breaks depend on the factory and specification. Do not assume that doubling the quantity will halve the unit cost.

Request quotations at the quantities you are genuinely considering.

## 2. How Does Order Quantity Affect the Unit Price?

The table below illustrates how to compare order quantities. It is a **quotation-planning template, not a market price list**. Enter actual supplier quotations before using it to make purchasing decisions.

| Order quantity | Quotation to request | Unit price | Total packaging cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1,000 boxes | Small production run | Obtain supplier quote | Quantity × quoted unit price |
| 5,000 boxes | Medium production run | Obtain supplier quote | Quantity × quoted unit price |
| 10,000 boxes | Larger production run | Obtain supplier quote | Quantity × quoted unit price |

Ask manufacturers to quote the same dimensions, board specification, printing and delivery terms at all three quantities.

You can then compare how the unit price changes as the order volume increases.

Also consider storage costs, cash tied up in inventory and the possibility that packaging designs may change. A lower unit price is not always worth purchasing more boxes than your business can use.

## 3. Don't Compare Unit Prices Alone

Consider two hypothetical quotations for the same packaging requirement.

| Cost component | Supplier A | Supplier B |
|---|---:|---:|
| Packaging unit price | ₹12 | ₹13 |
| Quantity | 5,000 | 5,000 |
| Packaging subtotal | ₹60,000 | ₹65,000 |
| Freight | ₹6,000 | ₹2,000 |
| Other charges | ₹3,000 | ₹0 |
| Total before any additional applicable taxes | ₹69,000 | ₹67,000 |

*Illustrative figures only. They are not actual manufacturer quotations or representative market prices.*

Supplier A has the lower unit price, but Supplier B has the lower total in this example.

When comparing actual quotes, confirm whether freight, taxes, tooling, printing plates and other charges are included. Check that the suppliers are quoting equivalent specifications.

## 4. How to Reduce Corrugated Packaging Costs

### Optimise the box size

Measure your product and any protective inserts. Oversized boxes consume additional material and may increase shipping costs.

Do not reduce the size so aggressively that the product loses adequate protection.

### Choose board strength based on actual requirements

A heavier board may be necessary for fragile, heavy or stackable shipments. For other applications, it may be possible to use a less expensive specification.

Discuss the product weight, stacking requirements and shipping conditions with your manufacturer before making changes.

### Simplify the printing design

Ask your supplier whether fewer colours, lower ink coverage or a simpler print layout could reduce costs without undermining your branding.

### Compare multiple quotations

Request comparable quotations from multiple suitable manufacturers. Standardise the specification so that price differences reflect supplier economics rather than differences in materials or scope.

### Plan repeat orders

If your demand is reasonably predictable, ask about repeat-order pricing and production lead times. Balance potential savings against inventory holding costs and design changes.

## 5. What Information Do Manufacturers Need for a Quote?

To obtain a useful quotation, prepare the following information:

- Box style: regular slotted carton, mailer box or another design.
- Dimensions: length × width × height.
- Quantity per order.
- Board construction and paper specification, if known.
- Printing requirements.
- Product weight and intended use.
- Delivery location.
- Delivery timing, if it affects your order.
- Reference image or artwork, if available.

If you are unsure about the board specification, state the product weight and intended shipping conditions and ask the manufacturer to recommend an appropriate option.

## 6. Compare Corrugated Box Quotations With Snaplogo

Finding suitable manufacturers and comparing quotations can be time-consuming, especially when each supplier requests different information.

Share your box style, dimensions, quantity, printing preferences and delivery city. The sourcing team can review your requirement, help identify suitable manufacturers and facilitate quotation comparisons.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is the price of a custom corrugated box in India?

There is no single reliable price without knowing the dimensions, board specification, printing, quantity and delivery location. Request a quotation based on your actual requirements.

### Are 5-ply boxes always more expensive than 3-ply boxes?

Not necessarily in every possible quotation, but 5-ply board uses a different material construction and may cost more for otherwise comparable specifications. The final price depends on paper grades, dimensions, quantity and manufacturing details.

### Does printing increase the price of corrugated boxes?

Printing can increase costs depending on the print method, colours, coverage, artwork and setup requirements.

### Are mailer boxes more expensive than regular shipping boxes?

They can be, especially when they require custom die-cutting, specialised structures or premium finishes. Compare quotations for the specific designs you are considering.

### How can I get an accurate corrugated box quotation?

Provide the box dimensions, quantity, board requirements if known, printing details, intended use and delivery location. Ask the manufacturer to confirm the full specification and total cost in writing.

title: Packaging Specification Sheet Template for Manufacturers
description: Use this practical packaging RFQ template to share dimensions, materials, quantity and printing requirements with manufacturers and receive more comparable quotations.
heading: Packaging Specification Sheet: A Template to Get Better Manufacturer Quotes
body:
When contacting a packaging manufacturer, the quality of your enquiry can directly affect the usefulness of the quotation you receive.

A message such as “I need 5,000 custom boxes” does not tell a supplier enough to calculate an accurate price. The manufacturer may need to ask several follow-up questions about dimensions, board construction, printing, delivery and intended use.

The same issue applies to flexible pouches, sachets, bottles and labels.

A packaging specification sheet brings the essential information into one place. It helps manufacturers understand your requirement, reduces unnecessary back-and-forth and makes it easier to compare quotations.

You do not need to know every technical detail before contacting a supplier. Record what you know, mark uncertain specifications as undecided and ask the manufacturer to recommend suitable options.

## 1. What Is a Packaging Specification Sheet?

A packaging specification sheet is a structured document describing the packaging you want to purchase.

Depending on the product, it may include:

- Packaging format.
- Dimensions and capacity.
- Material or board construction.
- Quantity.
- Printing and finishing.
- Functional requirements.
- Delivery location and timeline.
- Reference images or artwork.

The exact fields depend on the packaging type. A corrugated shipping box needs different specifications from a stand-up pouch or cosmetic bottle.

## 2. Copy-and-Paste Packaging RFQ Template

Use the following template when contacting a packaging manufacturer.

### General packaging requirement

**Product or brand:** [Enter name]

**Packaging type:** [Corrugated box / mailer box / flexible pouch / sachet / bottle / label / other]

**Intended application:** [Shipping / retail display / food storage / personal care / other]

**Quantity per order:** [Enter quantity]

**Expected repeat frequency:** [One-time / monthly / quarterly / undecided]

**Delivery city and PIN code:** [Enter location]

**Delivery timing:** [Optional, if it affects your order]

**Target budget:** [Optional]

**Reference images or artwork:** [Attach files or share a link]

**Additional requirements:** [Enter details]

**Specifications requiring manufacturer guidance:** [List any unknowns]

Please provide a quotation that identifies the proposed specifications, unit price, minimum order quantity, setup or tooling charges, taxes, freight, sample availability and estimated production lead time.

Please also confirm which costs are one-time and which will apply to repeat orders.

## 3. Corrugated Box Specification Template

For custom shipping boxes, mailer boxes and other corrugated packaging, include the following fields.

| Specification | What to provide |
|---|---|
| Box style | Regular slotted carton, mailer box, die-cut box or another style |
| Dimensions | Length × width × height, with units |
| Dimension basis | Internal or external dimensions |
| Quantity | Number of boxes per order |
| Product weight | Approximate packed weight |
| Board construction | 3-ply, 5-ply or other, if known |
| Paper specification | Required grade or strength, if known |
| Printing | Unprinted, one-colour, multicolour or reference artwork |
| Finishing | Any special coating or finish |
| Inserts | Partitions, dividers or protective inserts, if required |
| Delivery location | City and PIN code |

### Example requirement

**Packaging type:** Custom corrugated mailer box

**Dimensions:** 25 × 18 × 8 cm

**Quantity:** 2,000 units

**Printing:** One-colour brand logo

**Product:** Personal-care products

**Board specification:** Manufacturer to recommend based on packed weight and intended shipping conditions

**Delivery location:** Bengaluru, Karnataka

**Additional requirements:** Quote sample availability, tooling charges and delivery lead time.

This example provides a starting point for a quotation. The manufacturer should confirm whether the dimensions are suitable, clarify the board specification and identify any missing technical details.

## 4. Flexible Pouch Specification Template

Flexible packaging requirements vary substantially based on the product, required shelf life, filling process and packaging format.

Use this template for stand-up pouches, zipper pouches, flat pouches and other flexible packaging.

| Specification | What to provide |
|---|---|
| Pouch format | Stand-up, flat pouch, three-side seal, spout pouch or other |
| Product | Coffee, snacks, powder, cosmetics or another product |
| Pack size | Target dimensions and fill weight or volume |
| Material structure | Required structure, if known; otherwise request a recommendation |
| Thickness | Required thickness, if known |
| Barrier requirements | Moisture, oxygen, light or other protection, as applicable |
| Closure | Zipper, spout, tear notch or another feature |
| Printing | Number of colours, artwork and print requirements |
| Quantity | Number of pouches per order |
| Filling process | Manual, semi-automatic or automatic, if relevant |
| Delivery location | City and PIN code |

### Example requirement

**Packaging type:** Printed stand-up zipper pouch

**Product:** Roasted snacks

**Target pack size:** 200 g

**Dimensions:** Manufacturer to recommend based on product density and desired pack appearance

**Material structure:** Supplier to recommend based on freshness and shelf-life requirements

**Closure:** Resealable zipper

**Printing:** Custom brand artwork

**Quantity:** 5,000 units

**Delivery location:** Mumbai, Maharashtra

**Additional requirements:** Please confirm material suitability, sample availability, minimum order quantity and whether the quotation includes cylinders or other printing setup charges.

For food products, do not choose a material structure based on price alone. Confirm that the proposed packaging is suitable for the specific food, intended storage conditions and applicable regulatory requirements.

## 5. What If You Don't Know the Technical Specifications?

This is common for early-stage brands.

You may know the product, desired pack size and approximate quantity without knowing the board grade, pouch material structure or manufacturing process.

Instead of guessing, provide the information you have and ask the supplier to recommend suitable specifications.

For example:

- **Corrugated boxes:** Share product dimensions, weight and shipping conditions. Ask the manufacturer to recommend the board construction.
- **Flexible pouches:** Share the product, fill weight, desired shelf life and filling process. Ask the supplier to recommend a suitable material structure.
- **Bottles:** Share the product, required capacity, dispensing method and compatibility requirements.
- **Labels:** Share the container material, application surface, dimensions and exposure conditions.

Ask the manufacturer to explain any recommended specification that materially changes the price.

## 6. How to Compare Manufacturer Quotations

Once you receive quotations, compare them using the same criteria.

| Item | Supplier A | Supplier B | Supplier C |
|---|---|---|---|
| Confirmed specifications | | | |
| Minimum order quantity | | | |
| Unit price | | | |
| Printing or setup charges | | | |
| Tooling charges | | | |
| Freight | | | |
| Taxes | | | |
| Sample availability | | | |
| Production lead time | | | |
| Payment terms | | | |

Do not treat a missing cost as zero. Ask the supplier to confirm whether it is included, charged separately or not applicable.

Before placing the order, approve the final specifications and sample where appropriate. Confirm the production schedule, payment terms and delivery commitments in writing.

You can also mention which specifications are undecided, rather than delaying the enquiry until every technical detail is finalised.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What should I include in a packaging RFQ?

Include the packaging type, dimensions, quantity, material or board specifications if known, printing requirements, delivery location and required delivery date. Attach reference artwork where available.

### Can I request a quotation without final artwork?

Often, yes. A manufacturer may be able to provide a preliminary quotation using the packaging dimensions, material, quantity and estimated printing requirements. Final pricing may change when the artwork and specifications are confirmed.

### Do I need to specify the material before contacting a manufacturer?

Not always. If you are unsure, describe the product, its storage requirements and intended use, and ask the manufacturer to recommend a suitable material.

### Why do manufacturers quote different prices for the same packaging?

Differences may arise from material specifications, manufacturing capabilities, production quantities, printing methods, tooling, freight and commercial terms. Confirm that each quotation covers the same requirement.

### Should I request a physical sample?

For many custom packaging orders, a sample is useful for checking dimensions, fit, printing, material and functionality before approving bulk production.

title: Shipping Boxes vs. Mailer Boxes: Which Is Right for Your Brand?
description: Compare corrugated shipping boxes and custom mailer boxes by cost, protection, branding and use case to choose the right packaging for your D2C business.
heading: Shipping Boxes vs. E-commerce Mailer Boxes: Which Is Right for Your D2C Brand?
body:
Choosing the right shipping packaging is an important decision for an ecommerce business.

The box must protect the product during transit, fit your fulfilment process and support your packaging budget. For some brands, a straightforward corrugated shipping box is the most practical choice. For others, a custom mailer box offers a better presentation and unboxing experience.

But what is the difference between the two, and when should you choose each?

This guide compares the most common considerations to help you select the right format for your product and business.

## 1. What Is a Corrugated Shipping Box?

A corrugated shipping box is a box made from corrugated board, which combines flat liner sheets with a fluted paper layer.

A common design is the regular slotted carton (RSC), where the flaps meet when the box is closed.

Corrugated shipping boxes are used across ecommerce, logistics, manufacturing and distribution.

### Advantages

- Available in many dimensions and board specifications.
- Suitable for a wide range of shipping applications.
- Can be printed with branding or handling information.
- Often practical for standardised packing and fulfilment operations.
- Can be designed for stacking and transit protection when correctly specified.

### Limitations

- May require separate tape or other closure materials.
- Standard designs may offer a less distinctive unboxing experience.
- Oversized boxes can increase material use and shipping costs.
- The appropriate board strength must be selected for the actual product and handling conditions.

### When should you choose a corrugated shipping box?

Consider this format when your priority is reliable product protection, efficient fulfilment or shipping a range of product sizes.

It is commonly used by brands shipping household products, electronics, accessories, bulk orders and products that require additional protective packaging.

## 2. What Is an E-commerce Mailer Box?

An ecommerce mailer box is a packaging format designed to close around a product, often using a die-cut structure with integrated flaps or locking features.

Many mailer boxes are made from corrugated board, although the exact material and construction vary.

Mailer boxes are frequently used by D2C brands that want a branded presentation when customers open their deliveries.

### Advantages

- Can provide a more distinctive unboxing experience.
- May incorporate integrated closing features.
- Can be customised with brand colours, logos and printed artwork.
- Can be designed around a specific product or product bundle.
- May reduce the need for certain additional closure materials, depending on the design.

### Limitations

- Custom structures may require dies or other setup costs.
- Complex printing and finishes can increase production costs.
- A custom design may be less economical for very small orders.
- The structure still needs to be tested for the actual product and shipping conditions.

### When should you choose a mailer box?

A mailer box may be appropriate when presentation and branding are important parts of the customer experience.

Common applications include beauty and personal-care products, apparel, accessories, subscription boxes, gift sets and curated product bundles.

The best choice depends on the product, required protection, order volume and budget.

## 3. Shipping Boxes vs. Mailer Boxes: Key Differences

| Factor | Corrugated shipping box | E-commerce mailer box |
|---|---|---|
| Typical structure | Often a regular slotted carton | Often a die-cut, self-closing structure |
| Main priority | Shipping and product protection | Product protection and presentation |
| Branding | Can be printed or labelled | Can be customised for a branded opening experience |
| Closure | Often uses tape or other closure materials | May have integrated flaps or locking features |
| Custom tooling | Depends on the design | May be required for custom die-cut designs |
| Cost | Depends on material, dimensions and quantity | Depends on structure, printing and setup costs |
| Common applications | General ecommerce shipping and distribution | Beauty, apparel, subscription and gift packaging |
| Storage | Depends on design and how boxes are supplied | Depends on design and how boxes are supplied |

These are general comparisons. A well-designed shipping box can also provide excellent branding, while a mailer box can be engineered for demanding shipping applications.

Neither format is automatically stronger or cheaper in every situation.

## 4. Which Option Is More Cost-Effective?

The answer depends on the specification and quantity.

A standard shipping box may be economical when you need a functional box in common dimensions and do not require a specialised structure.

A custom mailer box may justify its additional cost when the packaging contributes significantly to the customer experience or allows a product bundle to fit neatly into one package.

When comparing quotations, consider:

- Material and board specification.
- Dimensions.
- Printing and finishing.
- Die or tooling charges.
- Inserts and protective materials.
- Closure materials.
- Order quantity.
- Freight and storage.
- Packing time and fulfilment requirements.

Compare the total cost of packaging a shipped order, not just the quoted price of an empty box.

For example, a box with a lower unit price might require additional inserts or packing materials. A different design could reduce those requirements, although the result must be verified for your specific product.

## 5. How to Choose the Right Box for Your Product

### Beauty and personal care

Custom mailer boxes may suit brands selling skincare, cosmetics or curated product bundles where presentation matters.

However, glass containers, liquids and fragile products may need internal inserts or additional protective packaging.

### Apparel and accessories

Mailer boxes can work well for premium apparel, accessories and curated deliveries. For lightweight products, compare the cost and practicality of a mailer box against a shipping box or suitable mailer bag.

### Electronics and fragile products

Prioritise product protection, cushioning, fit and handling requirements. The right solution may combine a corrugated outer box with an internal insert or protective packaging.

### Food and packaged goods

The correct packaging depends on the product, the primary packaging and the shipping conditions. Corrugated outer boxes may be used to transport packaged products, while the product-contact packaging must meet its own suitability requirements.

### Subscription boxes and gift sets

Custom mailer boxes can create a more distinctive presentation, especially when the contents are arranged for an intentional opening experience.

Check the dimensions and protective requirements of the complete bundle before requesting quotations.

## 6. What Should You Tell a Manufacturer?

To obtain a useful quotation for either format, provide:

- Box style.
- Internal or external dimensions.
- Quantity per order.
- Product weight and type.
- Board construction or performance requirements, if known.
- Printing and finishing requirements.
- Inserts or dividers, if required.
- Delivery city and required timeline.

If you are deciding between a standard shipping box and a mailer box, ask the manufacturer to quote both options using equivalent dimensions, material-performance requirements and printing assumptions.

This gives you a more meaningful comparison.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Are mailer boxes stronger than regular shipping boxes?

Not automatically. Strength depends on the material, board construction, dimensions, design and manufacturing quality. Select the format and specification based on the product and shipping conditions.

### Are mailer boxes more expensive?

They can be, particularly when a custom die-cut structure, specialised printing or setup charges are involved. The actual cost depends on the quantity and specification, so request quotations for your requirements.

### Can corrugated shipping boxes be custom printed?

Yes. Depending on the supplier and specification, corrugated boxes can incorporate logos, brand colours, product information and other artwork.

### Which box is better for a small D2C brand?

There is no universal answer. A standard shipping box may be practical for cost-conscious fulfilment, while a mailer box may be worth considering when presentation is a priority. Compare minimum order quantities, setup costs and total landed cost.

### Can I use mailer boxes for fragile products?

Potentially, provided the box and any inserts are designed and tested for the product and expected handling conditions. Fragile items may require additional cushioning or a different packaging configuration.
